**Finding: missing** — no vendor insurance clause exists in the Agreement.

Investigation summary:
- A document-wide search for "insurance" returned a single hit (p0051), and it runs *against* us — insurance is listed among taxes, duties and shipping charges that Licensee must pay. It creates no coverage obligation on Licensor.
- The outline has no insurance heading. I read the full General Provisions section (p0144–p0160): governing law, compliance, assignment, attorneys' fees, severability, independent contractor, notices, counterparts, entire agreement, modification, force majeure, construction, representation by counsel — and no insurance subsection. Searches for "Licensee Data", "servers" and "host" confirmed no data-security/insurance provisions elsewhere.
- Licensor supplies and hosts the licensed FX platform and handles our trade data and Confidential Information, so the rule squarely applies. Total absence of coverage fails the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) and sits close to walk-away.

Redline (validated `ok:true`): new General Provisions subsection **(l) INSURANCE** inserted after p0159, requiring CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, term plus one year, and certificates on request — the playbook's preferred position, drafted on the `seed-insurance` precedent. The comment offers the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as a landing zone if the counterparty pushes back on the amounts.
